cues.en: One thing that I really like doing in my courses is to actually understand the why of everything.
cues.zh: 我教課很喜歡的一件事，是了解每件事的原因。

cues.en: Everything that we learn, there should be a reason we're learning it right.
cues.zh: 學任何東西，都應該知道為什麼，對吧？

cues.en: And you might be asking yourself, why do we even care about machine learning?
cues.zh: 你可能在想，為什麼要關心機器學習？

cues.en: How is that useful and how do we get here?
cues.zh: 它有什麼用，又是怎麼發展到現在？

cues.en: Well, if you think about a business, because most technology evolves from business needs.
cues.zh: 想想企業，因為多數技術都隨商業需求演進。

cues.en: We have the advent of computers and the ability for businesses to use computers to do things really, really fast and efficiently so that they gain an edge.
cues.zh: 電腦出現後，企業能快速、有效地完成工作，取得競爭優勢。

cues.en: And then we got spreadsheets, spreadsheets like Excel files and CSV files where amazing, because we
cues.zh: 接著有試算表，像 Excel 與 CSV 檔，非常方便，因為可以，

cues.en: can store data that businesses generate such as maybe customer data into an Excel file.
cues.zh: 把企業產生的資料，例如客戶資訊，存進 Excel。

cues.en: And then people got really, really good at analyzing these CSV files, these spreadsheets to make business
cues.zh: 後來大家越來越擅長分析 CSV 與試算表，進行商業，

cues.en: decisions, maybe forecasting that December sales are going to be high because while the past two years we've had really high December sales because of Christmas.
cues.zh: 決策；例如預測 12 月銷售會很高，因為過去兩年都因聖誕節而有高銷量。

cues.en: And then as companies got more and more data, we started getting this idea of relational databases.
cues.zh: 公司資料越來越多，開始有了關聯式資料庫。

cues.en: Spreadsheets were great.
cues.zh: 試算表很好用。

cues.en: CSV files were great.
cues.zh: CSV 也很好。

cues.en: But we started getting more and more information and data and we needed a better way to organize things.
cues.zh: 但資訊與資料越來越多，需要更好的整理方法。

cues.en: To understand things from our data.
cues.zh: 才能理解資料。

cues.en: That's when we got things like MySQL.
cues.zh: 因此有了 MySQL 等工具。

cues.en: Which allowed us, instead of using spreadsheets, to use a language called SQL, to read information
cues.zh: 不用試算表，而是用 SQL 這種語言，從資料庫讀取，

cues.en: from our database, write information to our database, but similar to spreadsheets, use the data that
cues.zh: 資訊，或寫入資訊；但仍與試算表相似，利用，

cues.en: we gathered from the business to make business decisions so that our business becomes even more profitable.
cues.zh: 企業蒐集的資料做決策，讓企業更有獲利能力。

cues.en: And then in two thousandths, we have this fancy term of big data.
cues.zh: 接著到了 2000 年代，出現大數據這個熱門名詞。

cues.en: We had big companies like Facebook, Amazon, Twitter.
cues.zh: 有 Facebook、Amazon、Twitter，

cues.en: Google that started accumulating more and more data.
cues.zh: Google 等大公司，開始累積越來越多資料。

cues.en: An insane amount of data that you simply couldn't contain in a spreadsheet.
cues.zh: 資料量龐大到無法只放進試算表。

cues.en: User Actions.
cues.zh: 使用者行為。

cues.en: User likes user purchasing histories.
cues.zh: 按讚與購買紀錄。

cues.en: This idea of big data meant that we had so much data.
cues.zh: 大數據表示有非常多資料。

cues.en: These companies had so much data, and sometimes unlike relational databases, which had to be a structured form of data.
cues.zh: 這些公司資料極多，有時不像關聯式資料庫，需要結構化資料。

cues.en: Sometimes we got really messy, unstructured data.
cues.zh: 有時取得的資料很雜亂，沒有結構。

cues.en: And that's when we started getting this idea of NoSQL, where things like MongoDB came into existence,
cues.zh: 因此有了 NoSQL，MongoDB 等工具出現。

cues.en: where you can store unstructured data and hopefully make business decisions out of that.
cues.zh: 能儲存非結構化資料，希望再據此做商業決策。

cues.en: Maybe if you were Amazon, you can use customer's purchasing history to recommend different products.
cues.zh: 例如 Amazon 可以用客戶購買紀錄推薦不同商品。

cues.en: And ever since then, this idea of data getting more and more data has turned us into using machine learning.
cues.zh: 從那時起，資料越來越多，促使我們使用機器學習。

cues.en: Because at some point we have so much data that as humans we can't just look like we did at spreadsheets and look at columns and rows and make business decisions.
cues.zh: 因為到某個程度，人類無法再像看試算表一樣，查看欄與列就做決策。

cues.en: I mean, we still could, but then we'd be wasting all this data that we've been getting over the years.
cues.zh: 其實仍可以，但會浪費多年累積的大量資料。

cues.en: So companies like Facebook and Google that collect massive amounts of data every single day are turning to things like machine learning so that instead of humans looking at the data and trying to figure things
cues.zh: Facebook、Google 每天蒐集龐大資料，開始採用機器學習；不再讓人查看資料、試著，

cues.en: out, we give this data to machines so that they're better able, even better than humans to make business decisions.
cues.zh: 找出答案，而是把資料交給機器，讓它更有效，甚至比人類更擅長商業決策。

cues.en: And this idea of machine learning really came to be because of this growth in data that we received
cues.zh: 機器學習的發展，一方面來自企業提供的資料，

cues.en: from businesses, as well as the improvements in CPUs, GPUs, that is, graphical processing units and computer advancements.
cues.zh: 不斷成長，另一方面是 CPU、GPU，也就是圖形處理器，以及電腦技術的進步。

cues.en: So using the massive amounts of data and massive improvements in computation, we can use these machines
cues.zh: 資料量龐大，加上運算能力大幅進步，就能把，

cues.en: to give them this big data and make decision for us, just like we used to with spreadsheets.
cues.zh: 大數據交給機器，替我們做決策，如同過去使用試算表。

cues.en: Now, this is a simplified version of how we got here, but I hope it gives you a reason as to why businesses like this idea of machine learning.
cues.zh: 這是簡化後的發展過程，但希望能說明企業為何喜歡機器學習。

cues.en: Now in this course, we're going to be using this framework.
cues.zh: 這門課會使用這個框架。

cues.en: And don't worry, don't get intimidated.
cues.zh: 不用擔心，也別被嚇到。

cues.en: You're going to get really familiar with this framework because, well, we're going to talk about it a lot.
cues.zh: 之後經常討論，你會很熟悉。

cues.en: But looking at this, just a brief overview.
cues.zh: 先簡單看看。

cues.en: What do you think the hardest part is?
cues.zh: 覺得哪部分最難？

cues.en: Can you guess?
cues.zh: 猜猜看。

cues.en: It's this first part right here.
cues.zh: 就是最前面這裡。

cues.en: Grabbing the data.
cues.zh: 取得資料。

cues.en: You see, amount of data is doubling every two years in our world with the Internet, all the mobile phones and connected devices.
cues.zh: 網際網路、手機與連網裝置，讓世界資料量每兩年翻倍；這是講者在課程中的說法。

cues.en: We're creating more and more data, but this data doesn't mean anything unless we understand it.
cues.zh: 我們創造越來越多資料，但不了解它，就沒有意義。

cues.en: Yes, we are producing data, but a lot of this data that we generate is unused.
cues.zh: 確實一直產生資料，但很多都沒有使用。

cues.en: And that's what data science is.
cues.zh: 這就是資料科學的問題。

cues.en: How can we use this massive quantity of data that is completely useless right now to something that is useful?
cues.zh: 怎麼把目前完全沒用的龐大資料，轉成有用的資訊？

cues.en: And not all data is made equal, right?
cues.zh: 而且資料品質不盡相同，對吧？

cues.en: Some are noisy, some are messy.
cues.zh: 有些充滿雜訊，有些雜亂。

cues.en: Where do we grab this data from?
cues.zh: 從哪裡取得資料？

cues.en: How do we find it?
cues.zh: 怎麼找到它？

cues.en: How do we clean it so we can actually learn from it?
cues.zh: 怎麼清理，才能真正從中學習？

cues.en: We need to understand what data is and then apply machine learning to it.
cues.zh: 需要先了解資料，再套用機器學習。

cues.en: And the industry is now evolving into these people that we want to be data scientists.
cues.zh: 產業逐漸需要這樣的人，也就是我們想成為的資料科學家。

cues.en: That is, people that can turn data from useless to use full.
cues.zh: 把資料從無用轉成有用的人。
